questions.q:
With reference to India's nuclear diplomacy, consider the following statements:
1. The CIRUS reactor, used for plutonium before the 1974 test, was supplied with Canadian assistance.
2. India is a full member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
3. Canada suspended nuclear cooperation with India after the 1974 test.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: plutonium from CIRUS, built with Canadian help, went into the 1974 test, and Canada then suspended cooperation for decades, which makes the 2010 agreement and the Cameco contract a major reversal. Statement 2 is wrong: India received a Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver in 2008 but is not a member, its application having been blocked. This history explains Canada's insistence on peaceful-use conditions and material accounts.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 10-12; CIRUS, 2008 waiver and NSG status are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to principles applied after the strike on a girls' school at Minab:
Principle : What it requires
1. Distinction : Separating military targets from civilian objects such as schools
2. Proportionality : Treating an object as civilian whenever there is doubt about its status
3. Precaution : Verifying targets and choosing weapons and timing to limit civilian harm
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are right. Pair 2 is wrong: the presumption of civilian status in case of doubt belongs to distinction. Proportionality asks whether expected civilian harm is excessive compared with the anticipated military advantage. A civilian object loses protection only if used militarily. Military necessity is the fourth core principle. Together these guide assessment of whether a strike near a military site could still be lawful.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's links with Afghanistan, discussed amid the Af-Pak war of 2026, is correct?
o: The Chabahar Port lies on the Afghan coast of the Arabian Sea
The Salma Dam stands on the Kabul River near Jalalabad and supplies water mainly to Pakistan
The India-Afghanistan Air Freight Corridor was designed to get around the denial of overland transit through Pakistan
The Durand Line was drawn at the time of Partition in 1947 to separate India from Afghanistan
questions.e: The Air Freight Corridor was created because Pakistan denies overland transit for Indian goods to Afghanistan, and its revival is suggested along with Chabahar. The Salma Dam, or Afghan-India Friendship Dam, is in Herat on the Hari Rud, not the Kabul River. Afghanistan is landlocked, and Chabahar lies in Iran on the Gulf of Oman. The Durand Line dates from 1893, drawn between British India and Afghanistan, and Pakistan inherited it.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 17-18; dam river, Chabahar's location and corridor rationale are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs on science cooperation in BRICS:
Year : Milestone
1. 2015 : MoU making science and technology a strategic pillar
2. 2021 : AI Declaration placing AI at the centre of cooperation
3. 2025 : Intergovernmental agreement on space research
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is right. Pairs 2 and 3 are interchanged: the space cooperation agreement came in 2021, while the AI Declaration came in 2025. Formal recognition of the science track dates to 2011. India's CSIR and Department of Biotechnology coordinate its participation through the BRICS STI and Entrepreneurship Partnership. As Chair in 2026, India has been urged to build on these foundations with stronger institutions.

questions.q:
After the Minab school strike, accountability under the International Criminal Court was debated. Consider the following statements:
1. Iran has ratified the Rome Statute.
2. The United States is a party to the Rome Statute.
3. Israel is a party to the Rome Statute.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Iran signed the Statute in 2000 but never ratified it. The United States and Israel also signed in 2000 but later told the UN they did not intend to become parties, and India has neither signed nor ratified. So the Court's jurisdiction is limited where neither the territorial State nor the accused's State has accepted it, unless the Security Council refers a case. This weakens enforcement of the war-crime rule on education buildings.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 54-55; Rome Statute status of States is static

questions.q:
With reference to core principles of the World Trade Organization, debated at MC14 in Yaounde, consider the following pairs:
Principle : Meaning
1. Most Favoured Nation : No discrimination among trading partners that are members
2. National Treatment : Foreign goods treated no worse than domestic goods once they enter the market
3. Bound tariffs : Duties not to exceed agreed ceilings
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three are correct. MFN and national treatment are the twin non-discrimination rules, one at the border among members and the other inside the market. Bound rates give predictability. The notes see weaponised US tariffs as violating MFN and bound rates, and coercing partners into one-sided deals. Developing countries were advised to resist any challenge to these foundations at the conference.

questions.q:
The Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister's visit to Singapore and Japan drew attention to para-diplomacy. Consider the following statements:
1. Foreign affairs is in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. The Ministry of External Affairs set up a States Division in 2014 to help States promote exports, tourism and investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Entry 10 of the Union List places foreign affairs with the Centre, so States must align with national policy. The States Division facilitates their outreach without transferring competence. Investment summits, Kerala's Gulf diaspora links and IIT partnerships with Japan show what is possible, while Tamil Nadu's stance on Sri Lankan Tamils and West Bengal's on Bangladesh show how State actions can affect sensitive neighbour ties.

questions.q:
Israel struck the Caspian Sea area in 2026, treating it as a supply route between Iran and Russia. With reference to the Caspian Sea, consider the following statements:
1. It has no natural outlet to the open ocean.
2. Azerbaijan has a coastline on it.
3. The Volga river drains into it.
4. Iran lies along its southern shore.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The Caspian is the world's largest inland water body with no natural outlet, fed mainly by the Volga from the north. Its five littoral States are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan, with Iran on the southern shore. Because it is enclosed and far from the Gulf theatre, it served as Iran's secure rear for supplies from Russia, so strikes there marked a significant widening of the war.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15; Caspian geography is static

questions.q:
LNG traffic diverted by the Iran war took the Panama Canal to top capacity in 2026. With reference to this canal, consider the following statements:
1. Like the Suez Canal, it is a sea-level canal without locks.
2. It has been in operation since 1914.
3. A ship passing from its Atlantic end to its Pacific end moves broadly from north-west to south-east.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Panama uses locks that act as water elevators to lift ships over the central part of the isthmus, whereas Suez, opened in 1869, runs at sea level. Statement 3 surprises many: because the isthmus bends, the Caribbean entrance at Colon lies north-west of the Pacific entrance at Panama City. The canal is about 82 km long and shortens voyages by roughly 8,000 nautical miles.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 21; Suez features and canal orientation are static

questions.q:
Indians were evacuated from Iran in 2026 with help from Armenia and Azerbaijan. Consider the following countries:
1. Armenia
2. Azerbaijan
3. Georgia
4. Kazakhstan
5. Turkmenistan
How many of the above share a land border with Iran?
questions.e: Armenia, Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan border Iran. Georgia lies north of Armenia and does not touch Iran. Kazakhstan lies across the Caspian and shares no land border with it. Iran's other land neighbours are Iraq, Turkey, Afghanistan and Pakistan. India's evacuation used civil aviation assets with help from Armenia and Azerbaijan, which border north-western Iran and so offered an exit route away from the Gulf theatre.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-14; Iran's borders are static

questions.q:
On the limits of para-diplomacy, consider the following statements:
1. A State Government can conclude a binding treaty with a foreign government with the Governor's assent.
2. Parliament needs the consent of a majority of States before legislating on a State subject to implement a treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are wrong. Treaties fall to the Union under Entries 10 and 14 of the Union List, so a State can sign only non-treaty arrangements such as investment understandings. Article 253 lets Parliament legislate for any part of India to implement international agreements, even on a State List subject, and no such consent is required. This explains why the Centre retains final control in foreign affairs.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 20; Article 253 and Entry 14 are static

questions.q:
With reference to the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), consider the following statements:
1. It capped Iran's enrichment in return for sanctions relief.
2. The United States withdrew from it in 2018.
3. It was endorsed by a UN Security Council resolution.
4. India was one of the negotiating parties to it.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 2015 deal limited enrichment, and the US exit under Donald Trump brought back sanctions, after which Iran went beyond the limits. Statement 3 is correct, through Resolution 2231. Statement 4 is wrong: the parties were Iran, the P5 and Germany, with the European Union. India was affected through its oil trade and Chabahar but was not a party, so the deal's collapse had indirect impact.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-5; Resolution 2231 and JCPOA parties are static

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT share a land border with Afghanistan?
questions.e: Afghanistan borders Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and, through the narrow Wakhan Corridor, China. Kyrgyzstan is separated from Afghanistan by Tajikistan. Since landlocked Afghanistan's trade with India is blocked via Pakistan, these routes explain why India's connectivity options depend on the Air Freight Corridor and Chabahar Port in Iran, both of which were affected in 2026.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 17-18; Afghan borders are static

questions.q:
Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz in 2026 raised questions under the law of the sea. Consider the following statements:
1. Transit passage through straits used for international navigation is set out in Part III of UNCLOS.
2. The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman.
3. Innocent passage in the territorial sea is a separate regime from transit passage.
4. A coastal State may suspend transit passage in its security interest.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct and statement 4 is wrong: transit passage must not be impeded and cannot be suspended. Statement 3 is correct: innocent passage, under Part II of UNCLOS, is narrower, and may be suspended temporarily in specified areas. Statement 2 is correct: the strait joins the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. This distinction explains why closure of a strait is legally more serious than limits on ordinary territorial waters.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-15; innocent passage under Part II is static

questions.q: The 'Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement', cited as a diplomatic boost for Pakistan, was concluded with which one of the following?
questions.e: The agreement is with Saudi Arabia. The UAE features separately as financier of the Libya deal and through its President's visit to Islamabad, while Turkiye is a defence-industrial partner. Qatar was a mediator in the Af-Pak truce. The arrangement feeds the concern that Pakistan is emerging as a net security provider in the Gulf, where India has deeper economic ties but less defence leverage.

questions.q:
India and Brazil signed an MoU on rare earths and critical minerals. Consider the following statements:
1. Rare earth elements comprise the 15 lanthanides together with scandium and yttrium.
2. The India-Brazil MoU is legally binding on both countries.
3. India's list of 30 critical minerals was published in 2023.
4. Every critical mineral on India's list is a rare earth element.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the MoU is non-binding, though it signals intent and can build investor confidence. Statement 4 is wrong: critical minerals are a wider category, including lithium, cobalt and nickel, with rare earths only one part. Rare earths are not truly rare but seldom concentrated, and China's roughly 60 to 69 per cent share of mining is the strategic concern behind India's diversification.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to Pakistan's arms exports:
Armed group or force : Description
1. Libyan National Army : Force led by Khalifa Haftar, based in Benghazi
2. Rapid Support Forces : Regular national army of Sudan
3. Sudan Armed Forces : UAE-backed paramilitary rival of the regular army
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is right. Pairs 2 and 3 are reversed: the Sudan Armed Forces are the regular army, which Pakistan may supply with Saudi financing, while the Rapid Support Forces are the UAE-backed paramilitary. This creates the risk that Pakistan may end up arming both sides of Sudan's war. It also shows how Gulf rivalry shapes the deals described as Pakistan's arms diplomacy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's response to the 2026 West Asia crisis:
1. India stopped buying LNG on spot markets to protect its strategic reserves.
2. The Department of Fertilizers began emergency global procurement, diversifying to suppliers such as Russia, Morocco and Canada.
3. Seven inter-ministerial empowered groups were set up as rapid-response teams.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 3 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India bought extra regasified LNG on spot markets to keep pipeline hydraulics running for priority domestic users, and spot purchases are unrelated to crude reserves, which it managed carefully. The long-term lesson drawn is to accelerate green-energy transition and permanently diversify critical supply chains away from the Persian Gulf, given the thin buffers in fertiliser and gas supply.

questions.q: Which one of the following instruments treats intentional attacks on buildings dedicated to education as a war crime, a point raised after the Minab school strike?
o: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
Convention on the Rights of the Child
questions.e: The Rome Statute lists intentional attacks on civilians and on educational buildings among war crimes. The Convention on the Rights of the Child, through Article 38(4), obliges States to take feasible steps to protect children in armed conflict but does not itself define war crimes. The Genocide Convention targets intent to destroy a group, and the Universal Declaration is a non-binding statement of rights, which does not address this conduct directly.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to West Asia's non-State armed groups, described as part of the 'Axis of Resistance':
Group : Principal base
1. Houthis : Iraq
2. Hamas : Gaza
3. Hezbollah : Lebanon
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 3 and 2 are right. Pair 1 is wrong: the Houthis are based in Yemen, while Iraq hosts Shia militias. Iran funds, arms and trains these groups through the IRGC Quds Force, building strategic depth. Each group's location matters: Hezbollah pressures northern Israel, the Houthis threaten Red Sea shipping, and militias threaten US bases, which explains why Israel made dismantling this network a declared aim.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-5; Vision IAS pp. 12-14

questions.q:
The India-Canada uranium deal of March 2026 rests on an earlier legal framework. Consider the following statements:
1. The India-Canada Civil Nuclear Cooperation Agreement was signed before the Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver for India.
2. As a general rule, reactors running on imported uranium are under IAEA safeguards.
3. India may use Canadian uranium for peaceful nuclear explosions, provided it furnishes fissionable material accounts.
4. Signing the NPT was a condition India had to fulfil for the waiver.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct; reactors on domestic uranium stay outside safeguards, which keeps the strategic programme separate. Statement 1 reverses the order: the 2008 waiver came first and the 2010 agreement followed. Statement 3 is wrong: Canadian material may be used only for peaceful, non-explosive purposes, with the accounts serving as a tracking ledger. Statement 4 is wrong: the waiver allowed nuclear trade although India has not signed the NPT.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 18-20; Shankar IAS pp. 10-12; waiver year is static

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Eritrea
2. Oman
3. Sudan
4. Yemen
Which of the above have a coastline on the Red Sea?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Eritrea, Sudan and Yemen are on the Red Sea, along with Egypt, Saudi Arabia and others. Oman lies on the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, close to Hormuz but not on the Red Sea. The Red Sea joins the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal and opens to the ocean through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden, carrying about 12 per cent of world trade, so it forms a second vulnerable chokepoint.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15; littoral States are static

questions.q:
With reference to Article 51 of the UN Charter, consider the following statements:
1. Measures taken in self-defence must be reported immediately to the Security Council.
2. The right continues only until the Council has taken measures needed to maintain peace and security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are in the text of Article 51 and limit a right that is otherwise described as inherent. Self-defence is thus a provisional exception to the ban on force in Article 2(4), and the Council remains the primary authority. This explains why reference to Article 51 in Resolution 2817 was so significant in the Iran war, and why rival claims of anticipatory self-defence remain so contested.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-14; text of Article 51 is static

questions.q:
With reference to outcomes of the Canadian Prime Minister's visit to India in March 2026, consider the following pairs:
Area : Outcome
1. Multilateral : Canada to join the Global Biofuels Alliance and the International Solar Alliance
2. Food : Joint Pulse Protein Centre of Excellence at IARI, Pusa
3. Education and research : AICTE-Mitacs partnership
4. Minilateral : India-Canada-Japan trilateral cooperation
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are right. Pair 2 is wrong: the Declaration of Intent places the Pulse Protein Centre of Excellence at NIFTEM-Kundli, the food-technology institute, not at IARI. Pair 4 is wrong: the trilateral mentioned is India-Canada-Australia. Other outcomes included MoUs on critical minerals and renewable energy, a Defence Dialogue and a Parliamentary Friendship Group, together signalling normalisation after the diplomatic rupture of 2023.

questions.q:
Pakistan reportedly finalised its largest arms deal with Libya in 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The buyer is the Benghazi-based Libyan National Army.
2. The JF-17 aircraft is built entirely from Pakistani-origin components.
3. The deal is reportedly financed by the UAE, a long-time backer of Khalifa Haftar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the deal is financed from outside, showing the fragile dependence of such buyers on Gulf money. Statement 2 is wrong: the JF-17 was developed with China, uses a Russian engine and carries some Turkish missiles, and only about 25 are made a year, which is a real capacity limit. A UN arms embargo on Libya adds legal risk to the arrangement.

questions.q:
The legality of the 2026 strikes on Iran was debated under the UN Charter. Consider the following statements:
1. Article 2(4) bars the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of a State.
2. Article 51 in express words permits force against threats that may arise in future.
3. Protecting a people from their own government is a recognised ground for a State to use force unilaterally under the Charter.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 51 speaks of an armed attack occurring; anticipatory self-defence is a contested claim, said to require intent, capability and necessity. Statement 3 is wrong: neither regime change nor protection of a population is a recognised Charter ground for unilateral force, and the Security Council alone can authorise force in response to breaches of peace. Shankar's analysis applies these tests to find the imminent-threat claim weak.

questions.q:
With reference to India's critical-minerals policy, consider the following statements:
1. The MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 lets the Centre auction critical and strategic mineral blocks.
2. Customs duties have been cut on some critical minerals and on scrap and waste used for recovery.
3. KABIL explores acquisitions of mineral assets overseas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The 2023 amendment empowered the Centre to auction critical and strategic blocks, with several rounds held by September 2025. Duty cuts on minerals and on scrap support recovery and recycling. KABIL has been looking at assets in Argentina and Chile. The National Critical Mineral Mission, launched in January 2025, covers the whole chain from exploration to recovery, and India aims to begin rare-earth magnet production by end-2026.

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium and IOS SAGAR, whose second deployment drew 16 member countries, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the Indian Navy in 2008.
2. Under IOS SAGAR, personnel of friendly navies train and sail together on an Indian naval ship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Symposium was an Indian initiative in 2008, bringing together navies of Indian Ocean littoral States. The deployment is aimed at building interoperability, and 16 countries took part in its second edition. It is a low-cost way of acting on the idea of security and growth for all, and it adds to India's standing as a preferred security partner in the region.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 22; IONS launch is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Site in news : Country or countries
1. South Pars gas field : Iran and Saudi Arabia
2. Dimona, in the Negev desert : Israel
3. Ras Laffan Industrial City : United Arab Emirates
4. Natanz enrichment facility : Iran
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 4 are right: Dimona hosts Israel's nuclear facility, and the IAEA urged maximum restraint after a reported strike nearby; Natanz is a fortified Iranian enrichment site. Pair 1 is wrong: South Pars is shared by Iran and Qatar, forming the world's largest natural-gas field. Pair 3 is wrong: Ras Laffan is Qatar's main gas facility, so damage there directly affects the global LNG market and India's supplies.

questions.q:
With reference to West Asian groupings and corridors disrupted by the 2026 war, consider the following statements:
1. The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor was announced on the sidelines of the G20 Summit in New Delhi in 2023.
2. Saudi Arabia is a member of the I2U2 grouping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct, and the corridor is described as functionally paralysed by the war. Statement 2 is wrong: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the US; Saudi Arabia is not a member, though the UAE's Abraham Accords with Israel made such a format possible. Advancing these arrangements is listed among US geo-economic motives, alongside securing energy flows and managing oil prices.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-14; IMEC's 2023 announcement is static

questions.q:
With reference to Sri Lankan ports marked in news on the Trincomalee project, consider the following pairs:
Port : Coast
1. Kankesanthurai : Northern
2. Oluvil : Western
3. Hambantota : Southern
4. Colombo : Western
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 2 is wrong: Oluvil is on the eastern coast, as is Trincomalee to its north. Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are right: Kankesanthurai lies near Jaffna, Hambantota faces the southern sea lanes, and Colombo is the main western port. Trincomalee's value lies in its natural harbour near key Indian Ocean lanes, and the Tank Farm agreement of 2022 fits Neighbourhood First and MAHASAGAR.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 21; port coasts are static

questions.q:
With reference to BRICS science, technology and innovation, consider the following statements:
1. A permanent BRICS science secretariat has been functioning for over a decade.
2. GERD, a measure of R&D spending, is low in all members other than China.
3. iBRICS is an innovation network linked to technology commercialisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the absence of a permanent mechanism is a key challenge, as rotating leadership limits continuity, and hence a secretariat modelled on the EU's Horizon Programme is proposed. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Technology Transfer Centre and Institute of Future Networks are other visible outputs. Weak funding and uneven capacity explain the slow progress in mega-science and ocean and polar research.

questions.q:
India hosted the 12th Steering Committee Meeting of the GlobE Network. Consider the following statements:
1. It was set up under the BRICS anti-corruption working group.
2. India's CBI and Enforcement Directorate are among its members.
3. Its membership is confined to anti-corruption authorities of G20 countries, with UNCAC parties outside the G20 kept out.
4. It is headquartered in Geneva.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: both Indian agencies are members. Statement 1 is wrong: the network grew from the Riyadh Initiative of Saudi Arabia's G20 Presidency in 2020 and was established in 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: it is open to authorities of all UN Member States and of States Parties to UNCAC. Statement 4 is wrong: it is based in Vienna, where UNODC, its secretariat, is located. Its Secure Communications Platform allows swift exchange of information.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The India-Brazil MoU on critical minerals does not make Brazil a member of Pax Silica.
Statement-II: Pax Silica is a US-led initiative to secure the 'silicon stack', which India joined in February 2026.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true but unrelated in logic. Brazil stays outside Pax Silica because a bilateral MoU creates no membership in a separate plurilateral initiative; the MoU is also non-binding. Statement-II only describes what Pax Silica is, covering raw materials through factories to computing and AI hardware. India's membership does not extend to its partners. The MoU may still help India to access and process minerals.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Pakistan's reported arms deal with the Libyan National Army carries legal risk.
Statement-II: Libya is under a UN arms embargo.
Statement-III: Pakistan can make only about 25 JF-17 aircraft a year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both supporting statements are correct, but only the embargo explains legal risk. Production capacity is an industrial limit, and it bears on whether delivery in 30 months is feasible without affecting Pakistan's own needs, but it has no legal effect. Sudan too is under an embargo. Reliance on Gulf finance and the rivalry between Saudi Arabia and the UAE add a further financial and geopolitical layer of risk.

questions.q: In three decades of the WTO, only two new multilateral agreements are said to have been concluded. They are the
o: Agreement on Agriculture and the Agreement on Trade-Related Investment Measures
TRIPS Agreement and the General Agreement on Trade in Services
Government Procurement Agreement and the Information Technology Agreement
Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
questions.e: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement are the rare results. Agriculture, TRIMS, TRIPS and GATS were all part of the original Uruguay Round package in 1995, so they are not new. The Government Procurement and Information Technology agreements are limited-membership accords. This poor record is why many countries turned to free trade agreements, and why some see plurilaterals as reviving law-making.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 47-49; Uruguay Round package is static

questions.q:
Yaounde, venue of WTO MC14, is the capital of Cameroon. Consider the following countries:
1. Chad
2. Gabon
3. Ghana
4. Nigeria
Which of the above share a land border with Cameroon?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Chad, Gabon and Nigeria border Cameroon, along with the Central African Republic, Republic of Congo and Equatorial Guinea. Ghana lies further west, separated by Togo, Benin and Nigeria. Cameroon sits at the bend of the Gulf of Guinea, linking West and Central Africa. This is a typical way in which a venue in news is converted to a map question in the exam.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 47-49; Cameroon's borders are static

questions.q:
Statement-I: A disruption in Hormuz hurts India's gas supply more quickly than its crude supply.
Statement-II: LNG requires cryogenic infrastructure and is held only in small operational volumes, whereas crude has diversified suppliers and strategic reserves.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both hold and the second gives the reason. Crude can be drawn from reserves and replaced from about 40 supplier countries, but gas systems have thin buffers because storage needs cryogenic facilities and India lacks large underground storage. This asymmetry is why gas and LPG disruption spreads quickly into fertiliser prices and kitchens, and hence energy security has become a central foreign-policy concern for India.

questions.q:
With reference to West Asian waterways, consider the following pairs:
Waterway : What it links
1. Bab-el-Mandeb : Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea
2. Strait of Hormuz : Persian Gulf and Red Sea
3. Suez Canal : Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: None is right. Bab-el-Mandeb joins the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden; Suez joins the Red Sea with the Mediterranean, so pairs 1 and 3 have their ends crossed. Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, which is why a Hormuz closure cannot be avoided by using the Red Sea route. The chokepoints work as separate pressure points on Asian trade.

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Algeria
2. Chad
3. Egypt
4. Nigeria
5. Sudan
How many of the above share a land border with Libya?
questions.e: Algeria, Chad, Egypt and Sudan border Libya, which also touches Tunisia and Niger. Nigeria does not: Niger and Chad lie between them. Libya and Sudan are both markets in Pakistan's arms push, and their shared frontier matters since weapons sent to rival factions, such as the Libyan National Army or Sudan's warring forces, can leak across the Sahel and Horn.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 5-7; Libya's borders are static

questions.q:
India backed Canada's entry into a regional body during the March 2026 visit. Consider the following statements:
1. Canada is to enter the Indian Ocean Rim Association as a Dialogue Partner, not as a full Member State.
2. The Secretariat of the Indian Ocean Rim Association is located in Mauritius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Canada is not a littoral State of the Indian Ocean, so it can engage only as a Dialogue Partner. IORA's Secretariat is in Mauritius. Other outcomes included Canada joining the Global Biofuels Alliance and International Solar Alliance, a Defence Dialogue, and a Joint Pulse Protein Centre at NIFTEM-Kundli. Together they reflect wider normalisation of relations after the 2023 crisis.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 18-20; IORA Secretariat location is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about uses of nuclear technology in India:
1. The Dhruva reactor at Trombay produces isotopes such as technetium-99m and iodine-131 for medicine.
2. Arihant-class submarines run on diesel-electric propulsion.
3. Small Modular Reactors, for which the Union Budget 2025-26 set aside funds, run on natural uranium like India's PHWRs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: Dhruva's isotopes serve diagnostics and cancer treatment. Statement 2 is wrong: Arihant-class boats are nuclear-powered and form the sea leg of the triad, ensuring second-strike capability. Statement 3 is wrong: SMRs are compact reactors using uranium enriched to about 3 to 5 per cent, and the Budget gave Rs 20,000 crore for them as options for remote sites and industrial clusters.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Material in India's nuclear programme) with List-II (Its role):
List-I
A. Plutonium-239
B. Uranium-233
C. Thorium-232
D. Uranium-238
List-II
1. Fertile component of the mixed-oxide fuel of fast breeder reactors
2. Fertile material of which India holds a large share of world deposits
3. Fissile material bred from thorium, meant to fuel later cycles
4. Fissile by-product of pressurised heavy water reactors that fuels fast breeders
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Plutonium-239 is the by-product of the first stage, in which natural-uranium PHWRs run, and it fuels the fast breeders. There it is mixed with uranium-238, the fertile part of the mixed oxide that breeds more fissile material. Uranium-233 is bred from thorium and is meant to sustain third-stage cycles. Thorium-232 is fertile, not fissile, and India holds roughly 20 to 25 per cent of world deposits, which is the logic of Bhabha's three-stage plan.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Meaning
1. SAGAR : Doctrine of Security and Growth for All in the Region, announced in 2015
2. MAHASAGAR : A wider framework building on the 2015 doctrine
3. IOS SAGAR : A chain of Indian coastal surveillance radars in Indian Ocean island States
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are right. Pair 3 is wrong: IOS SAGAR is an Indian Ocean Ship training deployment in which personnel from friendly navies sail aboard an Indian naval ship; its second edition drew 16 countries of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium. Coastal surveillance radars are a separate form of capacity-building given to island partners. Names sharing 'SAGAR' invite this confusion in the exam.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 22; Shankar IAS pp. 55-58

questions.q:
Statement-I: New multilateral rule-making at the WTO has been very limited.
Statement-II: Ministerial Conference decisions work by consensus, so any member can block them.
Statement-III: The United States has blocked appointments to the Appellate Body.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statements II and III are both correct, but only the consensus rule explains stalled law-making, since any single member can stop an agreement. The Appellate Body problem concerns dispute settlement, which is a different function: it enforces existing rules and does not make new ones. Only the Trade Facilitation and Fisheries Subsidies agreements have emerged in three decades, so many countries have turned to free trade agreements.

questions.q:
With reference to US military facilities in West Asia that came into focus during the 2026 war, consider the following pairs:
Facility : Host country
1. Camp Arifjan : Kuwait
2. Ain al-Asad Air Base : Jordan
3. Prince Sultan Air Base : Saudi Arabia
4. Jebel Ali Port : Qatar
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are right. Pair 2 is wrong: Ain al-Asad is in Iraq, as is Erbil airport, while Jordan hosts Muwaffaq Salti Air Base. Pair 4 is wrong: Jebel Ali in Dubai, UAE, is the US Navy's largest port of call in the Middle East; Qatar hosts Al Udeid, the largest US base in the region. Iran's retaliation against such bases spread the war across the Gulf States and Jordan.

questions.q:
With reference to the law relating to armed conflict, consider the following statements:
1. Whether a State may lawfully start a war is governed by the UN Charter, whereas the conduct of the war is governed by International Humanitarian Law.
2. International Humanitarian Law binds only the party that began the conflict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 states the classic split between jus ad bellum and jus in bello. Statement 2 is wrong: humanitarian law applies equally to all parties, whoever started the war, which is its whole point, since civilians should not lose protection because of their State's aggression. It does not apply to mere internal tensions or isolated violence. Its core sources are the Geneva Conventions of 1949, their Additional Protocols and the Hague Regulations.
questions.it: Jus ad bellum vs in bello

questions.q:
In the context of the US-Israel strikes on Iran under Operation Epic Fury, consider the following statements about UN Security Council Resolution 2817 (2026):
1. It condemned Iran's attacks on several Gulf States and Jordan.
2. It invoked the Article 51 right of self-defence in respect of Iran's armed attacks.
3. It authorised member States to carry out strikes on Iranian territory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The resolution demanded that Iran stop its attacks and affirmed the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence. Statement 3 is wrong: it was directed at Iran's conduct and did not contain a mandate authorising force on Iranian soil. Careless readers often confuse a reference to self-defence with Chapter VII authorisation, but Article 51 is a right that exists independently of any Council permission.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to India's energy-security measures:
Measure : Description
1. HPCL-ADNOC agreement : Long-term LNG supply from Qatar
2. SPR Phase II : New caverns at Visakhapatnam and Mangaluru
3. Mercantile Marine Domain Awareness Centre : Round-the-clock monitoring of merchant shipping, coordinated with the Navy
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is right: the Centre tracks merchant-ship incidents round the clock in coordination with the Navy. Pair 1 is wrong: ADNOC is the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, so the 10-year LNG deal is with the UAE, although Qatar is India's largest LNG source. Pair 2 is wrong: Visakhapatnam and Mangaluru belong to Phase I; Phase II is being fast-tracked at Chandikhol in Odisha and Padur in Karnataka.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 16-17; Phase I sites from Vision IAS pp. 36-37

questions.q:
With reference to the Afghanistan-Pakistan hostilities reported in March 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Operation Radd al-Zulm is the name of Pakistan's military campaign.
2. Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, which emerged in 2007, is the Pakistani wing of the Afghan Taliban and works under its command.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are wrong. Radd al-Zulm is Afghanistan's operation, while Ghazab Lil-Haq is Pakistan's. The TTP is a distinct organisation, though tied to the Afghan Taliban ideologically, socially and linguistically, and it is not under Kabul's command. Pakistan's charge that the Taliban shelter TTP fighters, which Kabul denies, is a central cause of the war, alongside the Durand Line dispute and Pashtun nationalism.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The West Asia conflict of 2026 reportedly cut about one-third of global helium supply.
Statement-II: Helium is recovered commercially during natural gas processing, and Qatar is a major supplier.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. Helium comes as a by-product of natural gas operations, so damage to Qatar's gas hub and Gulf shipping removes a large share of world supply. The effect shows how a regional war spreads into semiconductors and medical imaging, which use helium for cooling and inert processes, far beyond oil markets. That is why the war is treated as a supply-chain shock and not only an energy shock.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-14; helium's source in natural gas is static

questions.q:
With reference to China, as discussed in reports of internal strain in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The 'Polar Silk Road' refers to an Arctic shipping route between Asia and Europe.
2. Liu Shaoqi, a former President, was purged during the Cultural Revolution.
3. Deng Xiaoping's reforms ended the Communist Party's monopoly on political power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Beijing has framed the Arctic route as supply-chain stability and not geopolitics, reflecting caution. Liu's fate is cited as a precedent for present purges. Statement 3 is wrong: Deng opened the economy to global markets while keeping the party's political monopoly. Xi Jinping's anti-corruption drive since 2012 has combined anti-graft aims with power consolidation, including military removals.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India keeps mining its low-grade uranium even though imports are cheaper.
Statement-II: Imported uranium is restricted to civilian use, so it cannot supply the strategic programme.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are right and the second explains the first. Indian ore grade is only 0.02-0.45 per cent, and Canadian ore is 10 to 100 times richer, so imports are the economical choice for reactors. Yet safeguards limit imported material to peaceful uses, so domestic mining remains necessary for the deterrent and for the strategic programme, including Arihant-class submarines, even at higher cost.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Rare earth elements, though not geologically rare, are difficult to obtain economically.
Statement-II: They are seldom found in concentrated deposits.
Statement-III: They often occur mixed with radioactive thorium or uranium.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both explanations hold. Dispersed occurrence raises mining and separation costs, while the presence of radioactive associates adds environmental and regulatory burdens. As a result, supply depends less on abundance than on processing capability, which is the source of China's dominance of about 60 to 69 per cent of mining. This is why India's push and the Brazil MoU extend to processing, refining and recycling.

questions.q: 'Doubling time', flagged by a former head of India's Department of Atomic Energy as a reason for continued uranium imports, refers to the time
o: needed to double national nuclear capacity through new sanctions
taken by half of a radioactive sample to decay
a reactor takes to double its power output after restart
a breeder reactor takes to produce enough fuel to start another reactor
questions.e: Doubling time measures how quickly breeders multiply their own fissile inventory. At an estimated 15 to 20 years, breeding is slow, so the 100 GW goal for 2047 cannot rest on the second stage alone and needs large, stable uranium imports. Half-life, the time for half of a radioactive sample to decay, is a common confusion; the other descriptions are not technical terms used in reactor physics.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to Iranian sites in the 2026 war:
Site : Location
1. Bandar Abbas : Close to the Strait of Hormuz
2. Tabriz : North-western Iran
3. Parchin : Near Tehran
4. Khuzestan : Oil-producing south-west
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are right. Bandar Abbas is Iran's key southern port by the strait, Tabriz lies in the north-west close to the Caucasus, and Parchin is a military complex south-east of Tehran. Khuzestan at the head of the Persian Gulf holds most of Iran's oil. Together they show how widely strikes ranged across Iran, far beyond the fortified enrichment sites of Natanz and Fordow.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15; locations are static

questions.q: Developing countries such as India have been wary of a permanent WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions mainly because
o: it would end their Special and Differential Treatment in all sectors
they lose potential tariff revenue as more trade shifts to digital form
the moratorium bars them from framing data-protection laws
the moratorium obliges them to open data centres to foreign firms
questions.e: The fear concerns forgone revenue and policy space as digital trade grows, whereas developed countries seek permanence. The moratorium concerns only customs duties, renewed periodically since 1998. It does not require opening data centres, does not stop domestic data-protection laws such as India's DPDP Act, and is not linked to developing-country status, which is a separate fight given US moves against China, India and Brazil.

questions.q:
With reference to the World Trade Organization, consider the following statements:
1. Its Ministerial Conference normally meets every year.
2. It began in 1995, succeeding GATT under the Marrakesh Agreement.
3. Timor-Leste and Comoros joined it in 2024.
4. Its headquarters is in Geneva.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the Ministerial Conference, the supreme decision-making body of trade ministers, usually meets every two years; MC14 was scheduled at Yaounde for March 2026. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Timor-Leste and Comoros are the latest entrants, taking membership to 166, covering about 98 per cent of world trade. GATT of 1947 had been a provisional agreement, while the WTO is a full organisation with its own dispute settlement.

questions.q:
China's 'Polar Silk Road' drew attention in 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. China has no Arctic coastline, though it describes itself as a 'near-Arctic State'.
2. The Northern Sea Route, a key leg of Arctic shipping between Asia and Europe, runs mainly along Canada's Arctic coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: China is not one of the eight Arctic States but promotes Arctic shipping, presenting the Polar Silk Road as supply-chain stability rather than geopolitics. Statement 2 is wrong: the Northern Sea Route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, while the Northwest Passage threads through Canada's Arctic archipelago. The two routes are often confused, and the Russian route matters most for Asia-Europe trade.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 52-53; Arctic routes and China's self-description are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Mineral : Country noted for it
1. Cobalt production : DR Congo
2. Lithium reserves : Chile
3. Rare earth mining : China
4. Nickel production : Australia
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 4 is wrong: Indonesia dominates nickel, while Australia is noted for lithium production. Pairs 1, 3 and 2 are right. This geography explains why India's overseas arm KABIL looks to Argentina and Chile, and why Brazil, with large rare-earth and bauxite reserves and only about 30 per cent explored, offers a useful alternative to dependence on a concentrated Chinese supply chain.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Afghanistan does not accept the Durand Line as a settled international boundary.
Statement-II: The Durand Line, about 2,600 km long, was drawn in 1893.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the second does not explain the first. Length and date are mere facts; Afghanistan's rejection comes from seeing the line as a colonial imposition, drawn between British India and Afghanistan, that divides Pashtun lands. An Afghan demand for a Pashtun state linking Pashtuns across the frontier with those of the former NWFP and Baluchistan would, for Pakistan, claim much of its territory, so Pakistan treats the line as its sovereign border.

questions.q: India renewed a bilateral swap arrangement with Japan effective 28 February 2026. Which one of the following best describes it?
o: Japan buys Government of India bonds of USD 75 billion for infrastructure lending
India alone can draw yen from Japan against rupee collateral, up to USD 75 billion
Exporters of both countries can settle trade directly in rupees and yen through their commercial banks
Either central bank can swap its local currency for US dollars, up to an unchanged USD 75 billion
questions.e: The arrangement is two-way, and it is a line of US dollar liquidity, not a yen line. It acts as a financial safety net against balance-of-payments or exchange-rate pressure. It is not a mechanism for bilateral trade settlement, and it does not involve purchases of bonds. India has other arrangements such as the SAARC Currency Swap framework for 2024-27 and those with the UAE and Sri Lanka.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A plurilateral agreement at the WTO binds only those members that sign it.
Statement-II: Adding a plurilateral agreement to Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement needs the consensus of all members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct but one does not explain the other. Limited application follows from the voluntary nature of such agreements, while the consensus requirement is a separate condition for admission into the WTO rulebook. That second feature gives any member, such as India, a veto. India fears fragmentation of the system, and proposals such as Investment Facilitation for Development ran into this hurdle.

questions.q:
With reference to Canada, consider the following statements:
1. It shares the world's longest land border with the United States.
2. It has the longest coastline of any country.
3. It is the second-largest country in the world by area.
4. It is the world's largest producer of potash.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The border runs largely along the 49th Parallel. Canada's coastline and area are its well-known geographic features, with Russia larger in area. Potash ties directly to India's fertiliser security, alongside pulses in agricultural trade. Canada is also the second-largest uranium producer, which supports the Cameco contract for 2027 to 2035. These make it a natural energy and agriculture partner in spite of political friction.
